target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where diagnostic model-call event accounting still copies stream chunks and model-call event bases with object rest/spread on hot paths. Issue #91588 includes field evidence that points at V8 dictionary-mode `CopyDataProperties` work around the diagnostic stream byte-accounting path during long-running Gateway workloads.

Scope boundary: This PR only addresses diagnostic model-call stream copy/spread hot paths; it does not close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker or prove multi-day RSS plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change removes object rest from `responseStreamChunkByteLengthUnchecked()` and conditional object spreads from `baseModelCallEvent()` while keeping the same diagnostic event fields. The stream copy now uses a null-prototype target so an own enumerable `__proto__` stream-chunk field remains a data key instead of interacting with `Object.prototype` behavior.

This PR is ready for review for the narrow diagnostic hot-path mitigation because validation now covers focused regression behavior plus an inspectable synthetic runtime benchmark. Longer-running Gateway RSS proof remains outside this submission's current evidence.

## User Impact

Operators running long-lived Gateway sessions should get less diagnostic hot-path object-copy churn during model-call streaming. The change is diagnostic-internal and does not intentionally alter model responses, provider transport, or persisted session data.

## Breaking changes (if any)

None expected.

## Implementation

- Replace `{ partial, ...snapshotlessChunk }` on stream chunks with direct JSON byte accounting for own enumerable fields except `partial`, avoiding a snapshotless chunk allocation on the normal non-`toJSON` path while preserving JSON omission behavior for unsupported values.
- Preserve object-property `JSON.stringify` semantics for non-partial values, including value-level `toJSON(key)`, by serializing object/function values through a one-property null-prototype wrapper instead of as root values.
- Preserve root `JSON.stringify` semantics when a stream chunk exposes callable `toJSON` via own non-enumerable or inherited/prototype lookup: a rare proxy path hides `partial` lazily, and a descriptor-preserving fallback handles non-configurable/non-extensible shapes.
- Keep own enumerable `__proto__` chunk fields as JSON-serializable data keys without mutating `Object.prototype`, including the `toJSON` snapshot fallback path.
- Build `baseModelCallEvent()` once and assign optional fields conditionally instead of using conditional spread literals.
- Add regression coverage for partial getter safety, value-level `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key preservation.
## Labels considered

`P0`, `impact:session-state`, `impact:message-loss`, `impact:crash-loop`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:needs-live-repro`, and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` from #91588 were considered when setting this PR's narrow scope and draft status.

## Validation

Current PR head: `d5d7b45fd45d898fdca8ca7206846839d27f6093`
Proof baseline commit: `28a841472684eed2d98a1a277fcefc30855b580b`

GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof:

- `PR 99154 model diagnostic runtime proof` — passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28671500815
- Artifact: `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-28671500815-1` (`summary.md`, `baseline.json`, `head.json`).
- Environment: GitHub Actions, `ubuntu-24.04`, Node `v24.18.0`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- Head binding: artifact `head.json` records `commit=d5d7b45fd45d898fdca8ca7206846839d27f6093`, matching the current PR head.
- Edge behavior:
  - Baseline partial-getter edge failed as expected: `partialReads=1`, no byte count.
  - PR head partial-getter edge passed: `partialReads=0`, `responseStreamBytes=34`.
  - PR head own non-enumerable chunk `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, `partialReads=0`, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`.
  - PR head inherited/prototype chunk `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `35` bytes.
  - PR head non-configurable `partial` snapshot fallback edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
  - PR head own enumerable `__proto__` data-key edge passed: expected/actual `73` bytes, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
  - PR head value-level `toJSON(key)` edge passed: expected/actual `68` bytes, observed key `value`.
- Synthetic model-call stream benchmark:
  - 50000 representative non-delta stream chunks were drained through `wrapStreamFnWithDiagnosticModelCallEvents()`.
  - Baseline duration: `190.16 ms`; PR head duration: `161.02 ms` in this run.
  - Baseline and PR head both reported `responseStreamBytes=2911669`, so the diagnostic byte-accounting contract stayed stable.
  - Short-run RSS deltas are recorded in the artifact but are not used as multi-day RSS proof.

GitHub Actions/check read-back on current PR head:

- Passed: `CI` https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28671364666
- Passed: `QA Smoke CI`, `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-lint`, `check-guards`, `build-artifacts`, extension/package/runtime boundary checks, contract shards, and all node compact shards.
- Passed: `OpenGrep OSS`, `Workflow Sanity`, `CodeQL`, `CodeQL Critical Quality`, `iOS Periphery Dead Code`, `Real behavior proof`, and PR target helper checks according to the current PR status rollup.
- PR status rollup at this update time has no failed or pending checks.

Local pre-check only:

- `git diff --check` — passed with no output before push.
## Evidence source map

- Issue field evidence: #91588 contains public native stack evidence around V8 `Runtime_CopyDataPropertiesWithExcludedPropertiesOnStack` / dictionary-key collection and identifies the diagnostic stream chunk copy site.
- GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28671500815 compares the baseline commit and current PR head with a 50,000-chunk model-call diagnostic stream workload, plus edge checks for partial snapshots, value-level `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial`, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- Regression tests: `attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts` covers partial snapshot exclusion without reading `partial`, value-level `toJSON(key)`, own non-enumerable/prototype chunk `toJSON` behavior, non-configurable `partial` fallback, unrelated lazy getters, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key byte accounting.
- GitHub Actions/checks: current-head proof passed and current PR status rollup is green with no failed or pending checks at this update time.
- Local pre-check only: whitespace/diff check listed above.
## Data model / migration compatibility

No persistent data model or runtime storage schema is changed. The only test-file additions exercise diagnostic event byte accounting and do not alter serialized session state, vector/embedding metadata, migrations, or upgrade behavior.

## Risk

- Diagnostic byte accounting can be sensitive to unusual provider stream chunk shapes. The added tests and proof cover the relevant review edges: skipping `partial` without reading it, object-property value `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON` lookup/ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- The normal non-`toJSON` chunk path remains allocation-conscious: primitive values serialize directly, object/function values use one small wrapper only to preserve object-property serialization semantics.
- This does not address diagnostic maps, session retention, plugin retention, or other long-running RSS contributors discussed in #91588.
- The implementation avoids provider/runtime behavior changes and is limited to diagnostic event construction and byte accounting.
## Rollback

Revert this PR. No data migration, config migration, or persisted format change is involved.

## Docs updated

No documentation files were changed. The patch is limited to diagnostic implementation code plus focused regression tests.

## Related issue / PR

- Related: #91588
- Related: #97211

#97211 covers the same diagnostic hot path and has public review feedback around proof, scope, and `__proto__` behavior. This PR carries focused regression tests and uses non-closing issue references so it does not auto-close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker.

## Review context addressed

- ClawSweeper requested inspectable real behavior proof before merge. The PR body now includes the current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof run and artifact listed in Validation.
- ClawSweeper flagged stale proof/head mismatch in an earlier iteration. The current artifact records `commit=d5d7b45fd45d898fdca8ca7206846839d27f6093`, matching the current PR head.
- Review feedback flagged that the earlier byte counter bypassed callable chunk-level `toJSON` semantics. The implementation now preserves root `JSON.stringify` callable `toJSON` lookup for own non-enumerable and inherited/prototype methods while hiding `partial`.
- Review feedback flagged eager getter reads in the chunk-level `toJSON` snapshot path. The proxy path is lazy, and the fallback copies property descriptors rather than materializing getter values before `JSON.stringify` invokes `toJSON`.
- Review feedback flagged value-level `toJSON(key)` drift for non-partial object properties. The manual byte counter now serializes object/function values through a one-property wrapper so value-level `toJSON` receives the real property key.
- The proof compares the baseline commit with the current PR head, verifies partial-snapshot behavior, value-level `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, own enumerable `__proto__` data-key behavior, and records a 50,000-chunk synthetic model-call stream benchmark.
- The broader #91588 Gateway RSS/OOM scope remains open and non-closing; this PR still only claims the diagnostic model-call stream copy/spread hot-path mitigation.
## Not tested / Limitations

- No multi-day Gateway RSS plateau/soak proof is included here.
- The runtime proof is a GitHub Actions synthetic model-call diagnostic stream benchmark, not a multi-day production Gateway workload.
- Short-run RSS deltas in the proof artifact are recorded for transparency but are not used as evidence that this PR fixes long-running RSS growth.
- No claim is made that this fixes all memory growth sources in #91588.
